summary: GPU power capping from mixed-precision fallbacks caused autoscaler to shrink capacity and transient tenant starvation
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reported sporadic P99 latency spikes and temporary 5xxs from their dedicated pool during lunchtime traffic on 2026-03-12. Symptoms included: increased attach time to GPUs, evictions from the pool, and sudden autoscaler shrink events followed by tenant request timeouts.

Impact:
- Customer (Acme AI) saw ~20% of their requests return 502/504 during a 14:20–14:35 UTC window.
- Throughput dropped for their pinned routes; internal dashboards showed brief reduction in live GPU attachments for the dedicated pool.
- Affected production flows: low-latency chatlets and short streaming sessions.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity pool: pool-dedicated-us-east-3 (pinned to HW-family: gdx-48gb-mix)
- Models served: redwood/gpt-x-13b-fp16 (primary), fallback to fp32 when kernel hit frag or mem alignment issues
- Region: us-east-1, prod

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) Run a short-stream workload with many concurrent, 2–6 token requests interleaved with occasional long requests (1:20 ratio short:long).
2) Force mixed-precision fallback on some requests by sending slightly misaligned sequence lengths and forcing attention patterns that trigger a legacy kernel path.
3) Observe GPU driver logs and autoscaler telemetry over a 15–30 minute window.

Observed behavior:
- GPUs reported repeated power capping events in driver logs (power_limit_changed / pwr cap applied) leading to clock down events and reduced TFLOPS per card.
- Serving runtime noted higher per-request latency due to lower clocks and more kernel retries; metric: kernel_retry_rate spiked 3x.
- Autoscaler observed sustained reduced utilization and fired a shrink (scale-down) decision; scale-down removed a small number of GPUs which led to request failures while attachments were rebalanced.
- Customer's short streams experienced serialized queueing and a rise in 502/504 until the autoscaler stabilized.

Expected behavior:
- Autoscaler should not react to short-lived driver-level power events that transiently reduce clock speed; should consider thermal/power signals as unreliable for capacity shrink decisions.
- Serving runtime should prefer FP16 execution paths for pinned models without downgrading to fallback on short misaligned requests when avoidable.

Logs / telemetry snippets:
- GPU driver: "pwr_cap applied: 160W -> 120W; clocks throttled" (multiple cards, repeated ~every 30s for ~10min)
- Runtime metric: kernel_retry_rate: baseline 0.2 -> 0.65; attach_latency p95: 180ms -> 560ms
- Autoscaler decision trace: shrink triggered at 14:25:12 UTC with decision_reason: "sustained_utilization_below_threshold (5m)"

Attachments / Links:
- customer-provided logs: s3://acme-uploads/sup-250999/log-batch-14-20.tar.gz
- internal dashboard links: https://console.redwood.com/dashboards/dedicated/pool-dedicated-us-east-3?span=15m

Immediate customer-facing summary (first response):
- Acknowledge impact, set customer status to "We are investigating", provide workaround to pin model to FP16 variant and reduce concurrent short-streams while we investigate.

2026-03-14 10:00 UTC | Priya Singh (Runtime Eng): Root cause analysis complete. Filed long-term fix PR to improve kernel selection and to add driver-signals-safe heuristics in autoscaler: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821. Scheduling rollout window in maintenance next week.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Mixed-precision fallback kernels cause inefficient memory access patterns increasing instantaneous power draw -> driver power cap applied -> lower GPU clock -> throughput drop.
Hypothesis 2: Short-stream heavy fanout causes workload bursts that push card to peak power frequently; combined with fallback kernels, this breaches power envelope on older card revisions in pool.
Telemetry findings: Correlation found between driver power_cap events and autoscaler shrink timestamps. Power cap events preceded autoscaler shrinks by ~45-90s in most samples.
Kernel-level traces: Certain attention kernel variants used under fallback showed 18% higher GPU compute time on identical batch size compared to preferred FP16 kernel.

Autoscaler policy evaluation: current policy treats sustained_utilization_below_threshold over sliding 5m as reliable; however it does not cross-check driver telemetry (power/thermal) which made it act on transient hardware-level events.
Risk assessment: Without mitigation, repeated events could lead to unnecessary capacity churn and customer-visible errors for pinned dedicated pools under bursty short-stream workloads.
Related past incidents: see SUP-41258 (thermal throttle) for similar clock-down observations; however that incident was caused by ambient thermal conditions not kernel power draw patterns.
resolution_notes: Mitigation applied 2026-03-13 09:22 UTC: (1) Set autoscaler to ignore utilization dips coincident with driver power_cap signals for pool-dedicated-us-east-3, (2) increased pool min-replicas by +1 as temporary buffer, (3) enabled prefer_fp16 execution path for redwood/gpt-x-13b-fp16 in that pool.
Customer impact after mitigation: 5xxs dropped from ~20% to <1% during comparable load windows. P95 latency returned to expected range within ~2 hours.

Long-term fixes: PR #4821 updates kernel selection logic to avoid costly fallbacks for short-stream patterns and adds autoscaler cross-check to filter shrink decisions when driver-level power/thermal events are present. Scheduled rollout: progressive canary starting 2026-03-21 with post-rollout validation dashboards.

Follow-ups assigned: Runtime team to complete kernel selection improvements (owner: Priya Singh), Autoscaler team to add driver-telemetry gating (owner: Diego Martinez). Notify capacity-planning for potential hardware refresh for pool-dedicated-us-east-3 in next quarter.
Customer communication: Sent post-incident summary and planned timeline for fixes. Customer accepted workarounds and will monitor during next week. Ticket closed with customer sign-off on 2026-03-14.
